note: Re-quoted 2026-11-25 to the Open Word Bible (OWB), Amharic, Balanced edition (CC0; library/data/bible/owb-am-b.json.gz, read offline as owb-am), per the founder decision of 2026-11-18 (Amharic quotes OWB everywhere). This supersedes what the notes below say about the 1962 UBS Bible and about wording borrowed from other Amharic works: every `mined` row is now a verbatim OWB span in its block (exact OWB pieces may be joined with '…'); `self_rendered` rows are allusions and paraphrases left as the translator's prose, each with its `why`. Chapter 6's title, the verse's question, is OWB's too (ከሌሎች በላይ ከፍ ያደረገህ ማን ነው?).

Scripture authority is the 1962 Amharic Bible (UBS; NT revised 2003). Its New Testament is on disk whole (ebible mirror gracious-tech/fetch_collection, bibles/amh_amh; re-verified for this job: the NT books return 200, gen.usfm 404). The mirror carries no Old Testament, so OT quotations reuse the wording of an already-shipped Amharic work where one quotes the same verse (source_file names it) and are otherwise self_rendered in the 1962 register.

A `mined` row was re-measured against the finished text: an exact substring of at least 20 characters of the 1962 NT verse (or 25 of the cited corpus file) inside that block. Shorter or re-personed quotations are self_rendered, whatever the translator believed. Luke 4:18 sits inside a bridged 4:17-20 entry in the mirror, so the chapter-3 inline echo (which the English takes from Jesus' reading of Isaiah 61:1) reuses the self_rendered Isaiah wording of the epigraph.

The English quotes the ASV; per the Amharic teens editions the epigraph cites book and verse with no version label. Isaiah 61:1 opens with the corpus's clause (divine-healing.am.json) and is self_rendered from there; Psalm 10:14, 1 Samuel 2:8, 1 Samuel 3:18 and Psalm 55:12-13 have no shipped Amharic rendering and are self_rendered.
